title: On-chip laser integration for silicon photonics
bottleneck: Silicon cannot emit light efficiently because of its indirect bandgap, so every silicon-photonic chip needs an external or bonded light source (typically indium-phosphide lasers). Heterogeneous bonding, epitaxial growth of III-V materials on silicon, and alignment add cost, yield loss, and reliability risk. A truly monolithic, CMOS-compatible on-chip laser remains elusive.
why_it_blocks: Without integrated lasers, photonic chips stay expensive multi-component assemblies rather than single-die solutions, blocking the cost curve needed for photonics in mainstream compute. Data-center optics and future optical compute both depend on solving the source problem.
current_state: Hybrid and heterogeneous integration of III-V lasers on silicon is in production for transceivers, and quantum-dot lasers on silicon show promise. Monolithic electrically pumped silicon-compatible lasers are still research-stage.
